name: Santa Fe Institute
focus_areas: Collective Intelligence; Simulation and Digital Twins; Foundations & Taxonomies
description: Independent nonprofit research institute for the study of complex adaptive systems, historically foundational to agent-based modeling, network theory, and complexity science. Runs the Foundations of Intelligence program studying conceptual abstraction, analogy-making, and general theories of intelligence across natural and artificial systems.
size: Resident faculty, external faculty network, postdocs, and visiting researchers (exact headcount not confirmed)
key_people: Melanie Mitchell (Davis Professor of Complexity; PI, Foundations of Intelligence), David Krakauer (President), Jessica Flack, David Wolpert, Mirta Galesic (among many affiliated researchers)
funding: Philanthropic/grant-funded nonprofit (specific current figures not confirmed in search)

name: Future of Humanity Institute (FHI)
focus_areas: Foundations & Taxonomies; Threat Models; Collective Intelligence
description: Former interdisciplinary Oxford research centre studying big-picture existential-risk questions, including AI alignment, AI governance, and global catastrophic risk. Publisher of Drexler's 'Reframing Superintelligence' (Comprehensive AI Services / CAIS), already in the paper canon. Institutionally defunct as of April 2024.
key_people: Nick Bostrom (Founding Director, resigned upon closure); Anders Sandberg; Toby Ord (alumni, now at Oxford Martin School)
funding: Historically funded by Amlin, Elon Musk, the European Research Council, Future of Life Institute, and the Leverhulme Trust

name: Cooperative AI Summer School
description: Advanced 5-day program for early-career professionals already working in or studying cooperative AI.
key_people: Same leadership as Cooperative AI Foundation (Lewis Hammond, David Norman)
funding: Run by the Cooperative AI Foundation (already in this doc)

name: Simile
focus_areas: Simulation and Digital Twins; Persona Extraction
description: Builds AI simulations of society populated by agents grounded in real human behavioral data, extending the original 'generative agents' research (Smallville). Offers enterprise workflows for customer/market simulation.
size: Not publicly disclosed; enterprise clients include Wealthfront, CVS Health, Suntory, Telstra, Banco Itau
key_people: Joon Sung Park (CEO/Founder)
funding: $100M raised, led by Index Ventures; participation from Hanabi, A*, Bain Capital Ventures, and angels including Andrej Karpathy, Fei-Fei Li, Adam D'Angelo

name: Artificial Societies
focus_areas: Simulation and Digital Twins; Persona Extraction
description: Builds networks of AI personas (300-5,000+ per 'society') to simulate stakeholder and audience opinions for enterprise market research, comms, and policy testing.
key_people: James He (CEO/Co-founder), Patrick Sharpe (CPO/Co-founder)
funding: ~$5.35M combined pre-seed/seed: $3.35M seed led by Point72 Ventures + Y Combinator; $2M pre-seed with Kindred Capital, Pioneer Fund, and angels tied to DeepMind/Sequoia/Figma/Prolific

name: Softmax
description: Independent research lab building the science of 'organic alignment' -- the thesis that the kinds of agents that stay aligned with humans are the kinds that stay aligned with each other -- through multi-agent reinforcement learning. Developed Cogames, an open-source benchmark/package for social intelligence games where agents cooperate and compete.
key_people: Emmett Shear (Co-founder; ex-Twitch CEO, briefly interim OpenAI CEO in Nov 2023), David Bloomin (Co-founder; ex-Google/Facebook/Asana engineer, MettaGrid project), George/Ozzie Goldstein (Co-founder; ex-Hipmunk, worked in Michael Levin's biology lab on active inference)
funding: Supported by 'a small group of individuals and organizations' (not publicly itemized)

name: Google DeepMind
focus_areas: Threat Models; Collective Intelligence; Multi-Agent Alignment; LA Infrastructure & Protocols; Coordination & (Super-)cooperation
description: Google's AI research lab. Authors of 'Virtual Agent Economies', 'AI Agent Traps', 'Distributional AGI Safety', and 'Intelligent AI Delegation' (all in the paper canon). Co-leads a $10M joint funding call (with Schmidt Sciences, Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA, Google.org), 'Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World', launched June 2026, to fund research on emergent risks in populations of interacting agents.
size: Thousands of staff (exact multi-agent-safety team headcount not disclosed)
key_people: Demis Hassabis (CEO); Nenad Tomasev, Matija Franklin, Julian Jacobs, Simon Osindero, Joel Z. Leibo (authors on the LAS canon papers); Owen Larter (Senior Director, Policy and Public Affairs)
funding: Alphabet/Google subsidiary

name: ARIA (Advanced Research + Invention Agency)
focus_areas: Trust, Delegation & Accountability; LA Infrastructure & Protocols; Threat Models
description: UK government research funding agency modeled on DARPA, funding high-risk/high-reward technical research. Runs the 'Scaling Trust' programme (whose Programme Thesis v2.0 is in the paper canon) and co-funds the DeepMind-led $10M multi-agent AI safety call alongside Schmidt Sciences, Cooperative AI Foundation, and Google.org.
size: Small core staff plus Programme Directors leading each research programme
key_people: Ilan Gur (CEO); programme leadership for Scaling Trust (specific Programme Director not confirmed in search for this entry)
funding: UK government-funded (statutory body, ~GBP 800M committed over initial years per public announcements)

name: Schmidt Sciences
focus_areas: Threat Models; Collective Intelligence; LA Infrastructure & Protocols
description: Philanthropic science-funding organization founded by Eric and Wendy Schmidt. Co-leads and hosts the application portal for 'Scaling AI Safety for a Multi-Agent World', the $10M joint funding call with Google DeepMind, Cooperative AI Foundation, ARIA, and Google.org.
key_people: Eric Schmidt (Co-founder; former Google CEO), Wendy Schmidt (Co-founder)
funding: Philanthropic foundation (Eric and Wendy Schmidt)

name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
focus_areas: Financial Systems & Systemic Risk; Agentic Economies; Threat Models; Policy and Governance
description: International financial institution (190 member countries) actively researching and advising on AI's macroeconomic, labor-market, and financial-stability effects, including agentic AI's impact on payments systems, monetary policy transmission, and systemic risk. Publishes IMF Working Papers and Notes on these topics and integrates AI considerations into country surveillance.
key_people: Kristalina Georgieva (Managing Director); Sonja Davidovic and Herve Tourpe (authors, 'How Agentic AI Will Reshape Payments,' IMF Notes 2026/004); Era Dabla-Norris and Anton Korinek (AI/macro scenario planning research)
funding: Intergovernmental organization, funded by member-country quota contributions

name: Bank of England
focus_areas: Financial Systems & Systemic Risk; Threat Models
description: UK central bank. Publisher of the April 2025 'Financial Stability in Focus' report on AI in financial services, already in the paper canon, examining systemic risk from AI adoption and concentration in financial markets.
key_people: Andrew Bailey (Governor); Financial Policy Committee (issuing body for Financial Stability in Focus)
funding: UK central bank (statutory body)

name: Don't Worry About the Vase
description: Blog by Zvi Mowshowitz covering AI, policy, rationality, and other topics, posting very frequently with detailed weekly AI news synthesis. Wrote a dedicated piece on gradual disempowerment ('The Risk of Gradual Disempowerment from AI'), engaging directly with the paper already in your canon.
key_people: Zvi Mowshowitz (author; former Magic: The Gathering Hall of Fame player, ex-Jane Street trader, MetaMed founder)
funding: Reader-supported (Substack subscriptions); author states he receives 'generous, essentially unconditional, anonymous' philanthropic support

name: AI X-risk Research Podcast (AXRP)
description: Interviews with (mostly technical) AI safety researchers about their research, aiming to get a sense of why it was written and how it might reduce existential risk from AI. Has interviewed David Duvenaud (Gradual Disempowerment co-author) and covered multi-agent/collective-behaviour research topics.
key_people: Daniel Filan (host)
funding: Listener-supported (Patreon, Ko-fi)

name: AI Prospects
description: Blog by K. Eric Drexler on AI prospects and their surprising implications for technology, economics, environmental concerns, and military affairs.
key_people: K. Eric Drexler (author of 'Reframing Superintelligence' / Comprehensive AI Services, already in your paper canon; former Future of Humanity Institute researcher)
funding: Individual Substack

name: The Cognitive Revolution
description: Weekly podcast where host Nathan Labenz interviews AI innovators and thinkers, discussing the transformative impact AI will likely have in the near future. Has covered agent-to-agent economy dynamics and interviewed Zvi Mowshowitz on AI safety worldview and multi-agent-relevant topics.
key_people: Nathan Labenz (host), Erik Torenberg (co-host)
funding: Turpentine Media network; sponsor-supported

name: Import AI
description: Weekly updates on the latest developments in AI research (including governance), written by Jack Clark, co-founder of Anthropic.
key_people: Jack Clark (author; co-founder and Head of Policy, Anthropic)
funding: Individual newsletter (jack-clark.net)

name: LargeAgentSystems.org
focus_areas: Foundations & Taxonomies; Threat Models; Collective Intelligence; Agentic Economies; Coordination & (Super-)cooperation
description: Resource hub for the emerging field of Large Agent Systems (LAS) safety -- decentralised systems of AI agents with high-speed, complex interactions, often ingratiated with the real world and possibly including humans (e.g. agentic economies, societies, democracies). Covers threat models including distributional AGI, gradual disempowerment, and systemic financial risk from agent integration.
key_people: Stephen Elliott (Gigascale Labs)
funding: Self-funded

name: Large Agent Systems Safety (Slack channel)
description: Community Slack channel for discussion and coordination around Large Agent Systems (LAS) safety -- the emerging field concerned with making decentralised, high-speed, complex multi-agent AI systems beneficial to human well-being.
key_people: Stephen Elliott (Gigascale Labs)
funding: Self-funded

name: EvoMap
description: Agent-to-Agent (A2A) collaboration network implementing the Genome Evolution Protocol (GEP), letting AI agents package, share, and inherit validated problem-solving capabilities ('Gene Capsules') across models and organizations via a credit-based marketplace.
size: 128K+ agents and 1.5M+ assets recorded in independent measurement study (Ye et al. 2026)
key_people: Not publicly identified

name: Olas Network
description: Decentralized protocol (formerly Autonolas) for building, registering, and monetizing autonomous AI agents on-chain. Provides on-chain registries (agents/components as NFTs), a staking/bonding tokenomics model, and a Mech Marketplace for agent services.
size: 146 open-source repos; ~27-64+ live agent services reported at various points; Valory (core dev company) team size not disclosed
key_people: David Minarsch (co-founder, ex-Fetch.ai AEA stack)
hq_location: (protocol is chain-based; issuing company Valory Ltd.)

name: Bittensor
focus_areas: Agentic Economies; LA Infrastructure & Protocols; Collective Intelligence
description: Decentralized blockchain network structured as many interoperable 'subnets,' each an incentivized market for a specific AI/ML task (LLM pretraining, inference, data, image generation, etc.), coordinated via Yuma Consensus and priced in TAO.
size: 64-100+ active subnets as of 2026; thousands of miners/validators across the network
key_people: Jacob Steeves (founder; now also CEO of Affine)

name: Collective Intelligence Project
focus_areas: Coordination & (Super-)cooperation; Policy and Governance; Collective Intelligence
description: 501(c)(3) nonprofit R&D lab building tools and datasets (e.g. Global Dialogues, Collective Generation, Weval) for democratic oversight and collective governance of AI, connecting global public input to AI labs, governments, and standards bodies.
key_people: Divya Siddarth (Founder/Executive Director), Saffron Huang (Co-founder), Jasmine Wang (Co-founder), Zarinah Agnew (Research Director)
funding: Backed by philanthropic funding (specific amount not confirmed in search)

name: Metagov
focus_areas: Coordination & (Super-)cooperation; Policy and Governance; LA Infrastructure & Protocols
description: Interdisciplinary research collective building standards, infrastructure, and empirical research for digital self-governance, DAOs, and online communities. Runs DAOstar (DAO governance standards body) and Govbase (crowdsourced governance database).
size: ~1,700-person Slack community; small core research staff
key_people: Joshua Tan (co-founder), plus network including Lawrence Lessig, Ellie Rennie, Primavera De Filippi, Nathan Schneider, Michael Zargham, Kelsie Nabben
funding: Grant-funded (e.g. GitcoinDAO funding for MetagovDAO; various project-level grants)

name: Lida Safety Research
focus_areas: Threat Models; Simulation and Digital Twins; Policy and Governance
description: Small nonprofit dedicated to technical AI safety research focused on forecasting and simulation, particularly mitigating existential risk and gradual disempowerment; work feeds into AI governance and public education.
key_people: Not publicly identified in search results

name: Equilibria Network
description: Builds mathematical frameworks (phase transition analysis and related tools) to predict where multi-agent AI systems break down, and identifies control levers to prevent those breakdowns. Explores the design space of collective intelligence through simulation and mathematical foundations.
key_people: Not publicly identified in search results

name: Alignment of Complex Systems Research Group (ACS)
focus_areas: Threat Models; Multi-Agent Alignment; Collective Intelligence; Coordination & (Super-)cooperation
description: Interdisciplinary research group studying multi-agent systems composed of humans and advanced AI, across scales from individual agents to civilization-scale systems. Core research threads include gradual disempowerment, LLM psychology/sociology, hierarchical agency, and a general 'science of the space of intelligent systems.' Built InterLab, an open-source toolkit for multi-agent interaction experiments.
size: Small (core team plus researchers/engineers across three locations)
key_people: Jan Kulveit (Co-founder; PhD physics, Charles University; former Research Fellow at Future of Humanity Institute, Oxford)
hq_location: Prague, Czech Republic (also London, UK and San Francisco Bay Area, USA)
funding: Not publicly itemized (research budget cited in job postings, $80-200k USD compensation range per role)

name: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER)
focus_areas: Agentic Economies; Labour & Automation; Threat Models
description: US economic research organization distributing working papers ahead of peer review across all fields of economics. Publisher of 'Automation and Repression' (Acemoglu, Gitmez & Shadmehr) already in the paper canon, and of the volume 'The Economics of Transformative AI' containing 'An Economy of AI Agents' (Hadfield & Koh), also in the canon.
size: ~1,700 affiliated researchers (mostly academic economists with NBER affiliation, not direct employees)
key_people: James Poterba (President); Daron Acemoglu, A. Arda Gitmez, Mehdi Shadmehr (authors, Automation and Repression); Gillian Hadfield, Andrew Koh (authors, An Economy of AI Agents)
funding: Nonprofit; funded via government grants, foundations, corporations, and individual contributions

name: Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI)
focus_areas: Policy and Governance; Threat Models; Agentic Economies
description: Independent nonprofit research centre producing rigorous research on AI governance and fostering policy talent, spun out from Oxford's Future of Humanity Institute in 2021. Research spans international security, arms race dynamics, compute governance, and -- notably for LAS -- agent infrastructure and governance (e.g. recent work on private-actor vs. government roles in agent protocols/safety).
key_people: Allan Dafoe (Founding Director; now also at Google DeepMind); Ben Garfinkel (Director)
funding: Philanthropic; funders have included Open Philanthropy, the Center for Emerging Risk Research, and Effective Altruism Funds

name: Modeling Cooperation
description: Conducts research and builds software helping improve cooperation in competition for the development of transformative AI.
key_people: Not verified in search

name: AI Safety South Africa (AISSA)
description: Capacity-building organisation focused on developing skills, networks, and community for preventing global catastrophic outcomes from advanced AI. Drives the Cooperative AI Research Fellowship (with CAIF, PIBBSS, and UCT's AI Initiative), serving as both talent pipeline and research direction-setter for UCT's emerging African AI Safety Hub.
key_people: Not verified in search
funding: AI Safety Tactical Opportunities Fund and Cooperative AI Foundation fund the fellowship; fellows receive compute credits from Lambda

name: BlueDot Impact
description: Runs the standard introductory courses for people new to AI safety: Technical AI Safety and Frontier AI Governance, plus AGI Strategy. The Frontier AI Governance course includes a unit examining 'competitive dynamics between labs and states, power concentration' relevant to multi-agent/multi-principal AI ecosystems.
size: 4-7 person core team; 7,000+ alumni trained since 2022
key_people: Not individually verified in search
funding: $35M raised total, including $25M in 2025

name: 80,000 Hours
description: In-depth career advice organisation covering the world's most pressing problems, including AI safety, through a job board, problem profiles, and a podcast featuring extended interviews with researchers across the field.
key_people: Benjamin Todd (co-founder), William MacAskill (co-founder)
funding: Philanthropically funded (part of the Effective Ventures ecosystem)

name: PIBBSS Fellowship
description: 3-month interdisciplinary program connecting researchers from diverse fields with AI safety mentors. Runs a dedicated Cooperative AI Track (funded by CAIF) focused on projects aiming to mitigate multi-agent AI risks and enhance cooperative intelligence of advanced AI.
size: Up to 6 fellows per Cooperative AI Track cohort
key_people: Not verified in search
funding: General fellowship funding plus CAIF-specific support for the Cooperative AI Track

name: Cooperative AI Foundation
description: Charitable foundation supporting research to improve the cooperative intelligence of advanced AI, funding grants, PhD fellowships, and workshops; produced the field-defining 'Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI' survey.
size: Small core team plus PhD Fellowship cohorts and grantees
key_people: Allan Dafoe, Gillian Hadfield, Eric Horvitz, Dario Amodei, Ruairi Donnelly (founding); Lewis Hammond (Research Director); David Norman (Managing Director); Thore Graepel (Board of Trustees, Google DeepMind)
funding: $15M initial philanthropic commitment from the Center on Emerging Risk Research (now Macroscopic Ventures); additional $10M fund announced with Schmidt Sciences, Google DeepMind, ARIA, and Google.org

name: Center on Long-Term Risk (CLR)
description: Research, grants, and community-building around AI safety, focused on conflict scenarios as well as technical and philosophical aspects of cooperation between AI systems.
key_people: Not verified in search
funding: Runs its own fund (CLR: Fund) supporting projects addressing worst-case/suffering risks from AI
